overview: Metcash is Australia's leading wholesale distribution and marketing company, supplying and supporting an extensive network of independent retailers across Food (IGA, Foodland, Foodservice & Convenience), Liquor (Cellarbrations, IGA Liquor, The Bottle-O, Porters) and Hardware (Mitre 10, Home Hardware, Total Tools) banners. Metcash does not itself own most of the retail stores it supplies; instead it operates a low-cost warehouse/distribution model plus retail support services (merchandising, marketing, retail media, technology) that let independently owned stores compete with the vertically integrated chains Woolworths and Coles. The Group employs roughly 14,000 people, operates major distribution centres across mainland Australia, and reports for the fiscal year ended 30 April (FY26 results published 22 June 2026).

business_model.summary: Metcash earns wholesale/distribution margin on goods sold through its warehouses to independently owned retail banners, supplemented by franchise fees, retail media, and earnings from a portfolio of company-operated and joint-venture retail stores (mainly in Hardware). Revenue is a mix of low-margin, high-volume wholesale trading (~72% of revenue, down from 81% in FY20 as the mix diversifies) and higher-margin retail, franchisor and out-of-home foodservice revenue streams. Earnings are largely transactional/volume-driven rather than subscription-like, though long-dated supply contracts with Multiple Store Owners (MSOs) and banner agreements provide some recurring-revenue characteristics.

revenue_streams.name: Hardware & Tools (Mitre 10, Home Hardware, Total Tools)

business_model.customer_type: B2B wholesale to independently owned retail store operators (IGA/Foodland grocers, liquor banner owners, hardware trade centres/Total Tools franchisees), plus large Multiple Store Owner (MSO) groups (Ritchies, Romeo Retail Group, Drakes Supermarkets) and foodservice/QSR customers via Superior Foods and Campbells & Convenience
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Australia; distribution centres in all mainland states; minimal direct foreign exchange exposure

main_competitors: PFD Food Services / other foodservice distributors
competitive_position.market_position: Metcash is Australia's '4th force' in grocery, supplying independent supermarkets (IGA/Foodland) that hold roughly 7-10% of national grocery retail sales, versus a combined ~65-67% for Woolworths and Coles and ~9-10% for ALDI. In Liquor, Metcash-supplied independent banners have grown share to ~32.3% (up from 26.6% in FY20), making it a stronger competitive position than in Food. In Hardware, Metcash's Total Tools and Hardware Group (merged IHG + Total Tools) competes primarily against Bunnings, the dominant player, with Metcash's network positioned in trade/independent hardware rather than big-box retail.

moat_factors.description: National distribution centre network gives independent retailers access to buying scale and supply chain reliability they could not achieve alone, though smaller than Woolworths/Coles' vertically integrated scale

Multi-year agreements with large MSOs (e.g., Drakes Supermarkets extended to 2034) and franchise banner agreements provide revenue visibility, though concentration in a handful of large customers is also a risk
IGA, Cellarbrations, Mitre 10 and other established local banners carry community/local-store brand equity that resonates with value- and convenience-conscious shoppers

Independent retailers rely on Metcash for merchandising, private label, retail media, technology and operational support, creating moderate switching costs, though large MSOs retain leverage to vertically integrate or switch suppliers

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory tailwind from mandatory Food and Grocery Code of Conduct
moat_factors.description: From April 2026 a mandatory ACCC-enforced code and an excessive-pricing prohibition (from 1 July 2026) apply to Coles and Woolworths but not Metcash-scale retailers, which could modestly improve independents' competitive standing

weaknesses: Structural scale disadvantage versus Woolworths/Coles duopoly (~65-67% combined market share) limits buying power and pricing leverage
Customer concentration risk in Food from large MSOs (Ritchies, Romeo Retail Group, Drakes) and contract customers (AUR/Foodworks) who could vertically integrate or switch suppliers
Hardware pillar has underperformed for multiple years (EBIT down FY24, FY25, and normalized declines in FY26) due to subdued trade/DIY activity and margin pressure in Victoria/Tasmania
Structural decline in high-margin tobacco category (sales down 52% since FY21) has been a persistent earnings headwind, though this is now largely cycled
Lower operating leverage/thinner margins than integrated retailers given the wholesale-heavy revenue mix

growth_drivers: Diversification beyond core Supermarkets into Foodservice & Convenience (Superior Foods acquisition, Campbells & Convenience) — Foodservice & Convenience sales grew ~14-22% in recent periods
Total Tools and Hardware Group (TTHG) merger of Total Tools and IHG completed in FY26, targeting cost synergies and a return to 'mid-cycle' Hardware margins ahead of an expected market recovery
Sorted B2B digital marketplace scaling rapidly (~$4bn annualised sales at 1H26, ~$6bn by early 2026, ~30% of Group revenue) improving supplier reach and convenience
LocalEyes/retail media network buildout (470+ screens installed, 260+ campaigns completed) creating a new higher-margin revenue stream
Program Horizon technology transformation (core ERP/D365 build complete, deployment through FY27) expected to reduce cost-to-serve and improve efficiency once completed

Selective retail ownership/M&A strategy — recent bolt-on acquisitions (Steve's Liquor Warehouse, Holliman's Rural, prior Superior Foods, Alpine Truss, Bianco Building Supplies) and first supermarket acquisitions completed in Q4 FY26 as Metcash tests direct retail ownership
Structural tailwind from mandatory Food and Grocery Code of Conduct and 'excessive pricing' scrutiny of Coles/Woolworths from July 2026, which may support the value proposition of independents
Continued liquor market share gains (32.3% and rising) as shoppers favor convenience/localised offers over major chains

business.risk: Woolworths/Coles duopoly pricing and scale pressure
business.description: The two majors control ~65-67% of grocery retail and can leverage scale in buying and pricing that independents/Metcash cannot fully match

Subdued trade/DIY activity, particularly in Victoria and Tasmania, has driven EBIT declines for three consecutive years despite revenue growth from acquisitions; recovery depends on housing/renovation cycle turning

Large Multiple Store Owners (Ritchies, Romeo Retail Group, Drakes Supermarkets) and contract customers (AUR/Foodworks) could reduce or cease sourcing from Metcash, materially impacting Food segment volumes
Legal tobacco sales down 52% since FY21 amid illicit trade growth and excise increases; accelerated 5% excise concluded in FY26, removing a prior earnings tailwind from strategic buying gains

business.risk: Execution risk on Program Horizon and TTHG integration
business.description: Multi-year technology transformation (targeted completion FY27) and Total Tools/IHG merger integration carry cost overrun, delay and benefit-realization risk

financial.risk: Rising net debt and finance costs
financial.description: Net debt increased from $251.9m (FY24) to $577.4m (FY25) to $616.6m (FY26) on acquisitions and capex, with net finance costs up from $92.6m to $123.7m over the period; debt leverage ratio target band is 1.0x-1.75x

financial.risk: Credit risk on independent retailer trade receivables
financial.description: Metcash extends credit and trading terms to independent retailers; deterioration in retailer profitability/cash flow in a weak consumer environment could increase bad debt risk

financial.risk: Refinancing/covenant risk in a higher-rate environment
financial.description: Elevated interest rates and potential banking market volatility could increase funding costs or affect ability to refinance debt facilities on favorable terms

regulatory.risk: Mandatory Food and Grocery Code of Conduct compliance costs
regulatory.description: The code became mandatory from April 2025/2026 with ACCC civil penalty powers; while primarily targeted at 'very large retailers' (Coles/Woolworths) for excessive pricing from July 2026, compliance costs and supply-agreement requirements apply across the industry including Metcash
Ongoing excise increases and regulatory changes affect tobacco and liquor category economics; illicit tobacco trade growth also pressures legal category volumes
As a Group 1 reporting entity under Australia's mandatory climate disclosure regime, Metcash must now produce assured AASB S2 climate statements (first full year FY26), adding compliance cost

macro.description: Softer consumer sentiment, particularly evident in a subdued May 2026 start to FY27 before recovering, can pressure discretionary categories (Hardware, on-premise liquor) more than grocery staples
Hardware & Tools earnings are cyclically exposed to housing construction and renovation activity, which has been subdued for several years
Ongoing wage, energy and logistics cost inflation, offset partially by moderating product wholesale price inflation (1.4% in FY25 versus 4.8% in FY24)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian grocery wholesale/distribution is a large, low-growth, defensive market with structural duopoly dominance by Woolworths and Coles; independent retail (IGA/Foodland) has held roughly stable-to-slightly-growing share, aided by localisation and value positioning. Hardware/DIY trade activity has been in a multi-year downturn but management notes early signs of recovery into FY27. Liquor independents continue to take share from majors.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - Food/grocery wholesale is defensive and non-discretionary; Hardware & Tools and on-premise Liquor are more cyclical, tied to housing/renovation activity and discretionary hospitality spend
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - net debt of ~$617m (FY26) with variable and swap-hedged components; rising rates increase finance costs and can dampen consumer/trade-customer activity
key_input_costs: Labour costs across distribution centres and retail network

recent_developments.event: AGM and 18-week FY27 trading update: Group sales up 3.5% including tobacco (2.8% ex-tobacco); Food +3.8%/+2.6% ex-tobacco; Liquor +0.8%; Hardware & Tools +6.0%; tobacco sales up 11.7% as illicit-tobacco enforcement improved in some states; stock fell ~2.7% on the day amid cost-of-living/inflation concerns despite the positive update

FY26 full-year results: Sales revenue $17.35bn (+0.2%); EBITDA $761.7m (+1.9%); EBIT $503.7m (-0.8%, +1.6% normalised for one-off integration/strategy costs); UPAT $268.8m (-2.4%); final dividend 9.5 cps fully franked, full-year dividend 18.0 cps (73.6% payout ratio); DRP suspended from FY26 final dividend; net debt rose to $616.6m

Completion of Total Tools and Independent Hardware Group (IHG) merger into 'Total Tools and Hardware Group' (TTHG), duplication removed and scale benefits beginning to flow; business refocused on returning to mid-cycle Hardware margins

Acquired Steve's Liquor Warehouse (8 retail stores, Victoria/Tasmania) and 75% of Holliman's Rural Pty Ltd, expanding regional/rural customer base; completed first direct supermarket acquisitions in Q4 FY26 as part of a retail-ownership strategy test

1H FY26 results: Group revenue $9.6bn (+0.4%, +4.5% ex-tobacco), EBITDA $367.2m (+2.0%), reported PAT $142.2m (+0.3%); Sorted B2B marketplace scaled to ~$4-6bn annualised sales (~30% of Group revenue); LocalEyes retail media network reached 470 screens/260+ campaigns

Australia's mandatory Food and Grocery Code of Conduct came into full force (transition period ended 1 April 2026), with an 'excessive pricing' prohibition for Coles and Woolworths from 1 July 2026 — a modest structural tailwind for independents' competitive positioning

Superior Foods (foodservice distribution) merged with Campbells & Convenience to form 'Foodservice & Convenience', delivering rapid growth (sales +14-22% in various periods) and integration synergies in line with target

guidance.as_of: FY26 Full Year Results / September 2026 AGM Trading Update

items.period: First 18 weeks of FY27 (to early Sept 2026)
items.vs_prior: maintained positive momentum vs FY26 trend
items.notes: Broad-based growth across Food, Liquor and Hardware & Tools; Hardware & Tools led growth at +6.0%

items.target: Core ERP (D365) deployment beginning June 2026, targeted completion Q4 CY2026 / FY27
items.notes: Cumulative Program Horizon costs of $286.7m as at FY26 ($161.3m capex + $125.4m expense)

items.target: 1.0x - 1.75x (Net Debt / Underlying EBITDA less ROU depreciation)
items.notes: 1H26 DLR was reported at ~1.0x, within target band

items.period: FY26 actual: 73.6% payout; FY27 policy under review

items.notes: No explicit forward EPS or margin guidance range was disclosed in the extracted filings; management commentary is qualitative (trading momentum by pillar) rather than point-estimate guidance

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Doug Jones characterised the FY27 start as a 'steady start... reflecting softer trading conditions in May followed by a clear improvement in June,' with Food and Liquor subdued in May on geopolitical uncertainty and cost-of-living pressures before recovering in the following weeks. Hardware & Tools was flagged as continuing strong momentum, extending improved 2H26 performance into early FY27, led by high single-digit growth in Total Tools. Management emphasised 'attractive retail M&A opportunities,' balance sheet flexibility, and the TTHG merger positioning Hardware for market-recovery upside. No specific FY27 revenue, EBIT or EPS point guidance was provided in the reviewed filings; guidance is directional/qualitative by pillar.

bull_case: Diversification into Foodservice & Convenience (Superior Foods) and B2B digital (Sorted marketplace, ~30% of Group revenue) and retail media (LocalEyes) is creating new, higher-margin revenue streams beyond the mature core wholesale business

Hardware & Tools is troughing after three years of EBIT decline; the completed TTHG merger removes duplication, and management and analysts point to early signs of trade market recovery into FY27 (high single-digit Total Tools growth, improving 2H26 momentum)

Mandatory Food and Grocery Code of Conduct and 'excessive pricing' scrutiny of Coles/Woolworths from July 2026 could structurally improve independents' relative competitiveness and consumer perception
Liquor market share has grown from 26.6% (FY20) to 32.3% and continues to take share from majors, evidencing a genuinely differentiated, resilient value proposition

Consensus analyst rating is broadly Buy/Hold with price targets (~A$3.0-4.0) generally above the recent trading range (~A$2.8-2.9), and management retains balance sheet flexibility and appetite for further bolt-on M&A
bear_case: Structural scale disadvantage against the Woolworths/Coles duopoly (~65-67% combined market share) constrains buying power, pricing and margin expansion potential over the long run

Hardware segment has underperformed for multiple consecutive years and remains exposed to a housing/renovation cycle that has yet to convincingly turn, with FY26 normalised EBIT still down year-on-year in Victoria/Tasmania

Rising net debt ($616.6m FY26, up from $251.9m FY24) and finance costs, combined with continued M&A appetite, add financial risk in a still-elevated interest rate environment; DRP suspension may signal capital discipline concerns

Underlying profit after tax has declined for two consecutive years (FY25 -2.4%, FY26 -2.4%) despite revenue growth, indicating margin/earnings quality pressure from acquisitions' D&A, integration costs and softer Liquor/Hardware EBIT

Execution risk remains on the multi-year Program Horizon technology transformation (cumulative cost $286.7m and rising, completion pushed to FY27) and continued integration of recent acquisitions (Superior Foods, TTHG merger, Steve's Liquor, Holliman's Rural)
